# 630. Relative density of sets generated by fixed-parameter extrapolation

**Area:** Discrete geometry and aperiodic order

**Status:** ✅ SOLVED

**Last checked:** 2026-10-15

## Problem statement

For $`\lambda\in\mathbb C`$, let $`Q_\lambda`$ be the smallest set containing $`0,1`$ and closed under $`(a,b)\mapsto(1-\lambda)a+\lambda b`$, without taking a topological closure.

Set $`X_\lambda=\mathbb R`$ when $`\lambda\in\mathbb R\setminus[0,1]`$, and $`X_\lambda=\mathbb C`$ when $`\lambda\notin\mathbb R`$. Is $`Q_\lambda`$ relatively dense in $`X_\lambda`$ for every such parameter? Explicitly, is there a finite constant $`R_\lambda`$ such that

```math
\forall z\in X_\lambda\quad\exists q\in Q_\lambda:\quad |z-q|\le R_\lambda?
```

The radius may depend on $`\lambda`$. If the universal assertion fails, characterize the parameters for which it holds.

## Application

Relative density prevents arbitrarily large holes in a generated point pattern. Together with uniform discreteness it supplies the geometric basis for Delone sets and quasicrystal models.

## References

1. S. Fenner, F. Green and S. Homer, [Fixed-Parameter Extrapolation and Aperiodic Order](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-025-00816-4), *Discrete & Computational Geometry* **76** (2026), 1–74, Open Question 11.3 and Sections 6, 8–9.
2. S. Fenner, F. Green and S. Homer, [Extended manuscript](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.2889).

## Status review

Reviewed 15 October 2026 against the original target in [PR #109](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/pull/109). Every fixed extrapolation parameter outside[0,1] produces a relatively dense set in its full real or complex ambient space.

[Proof or source](../research/solutions/aim-630-extrapolation-relative-density/paper/relative_density.pdf) · [Independent AI review](../research/solution_reviews/2026-10-15-active-prs/630-review.md). The linked review records the exact scope and verification limits; this is not human peer review or Lean verification.

**Scope:** The generated set Q_lambda itself, using only finite operations, has uniformly bounded holes for every real lambda outside[0,1] and every nonreal lambda.

### Earlier review notes

The following historical notes are retained; the current decision and review date are given above.

**Known cases:** The source establishes relative density for multiple explicit real and nonreal algebraic parameters using covering and affine-embedding methods. Any parameter for which $`Q_\lambda`$ is dense in its ambient space also satisfies the requested property.

**Remaining target:** Establish relative density for every parameter in the stated domains, including the remaining discrete cases. The question concerns bounded holes, a different property from the separation of points in the discreteness conjecture. The June 2026 paper explicitly leaves the universal statement open.
